correctness.rationale: The characteristic-two companion expression expands to the given equation, and the q=2, b=1 specialization satisfies Lemma 9.2's smoothness hypothesis. An independent point count used X0=1 rather than X3=1: fixing X2=c separates an X1-polynomial b³+(1+c²)b²+c³b from an X3-polynomial (1+c)d³+c²d²+d; the remaining normalized charts were counted separately. The computation used independently constructed irreducible binary moduli and reproduced all 13 recorded counts. Independent integer Newton identities gave midpoint -43008, which forces the plus sign of the weight-two duality relation, and the degree-22 factorization agrees with the finding and the two redundant counts. The reciprocal degree-12 polynomial is irreducible modulo 13. Thus the irreducible normalized factor cannot have a cyclotomic root, as its constant term is 1 but its quadratic coefficient is 1/2. The other normalized roots are six copies of 1 and two copies each of i and -i. The Tate theorem over the indicated extensions gives exactly the claimed ranks. The lower valuation hull in descending reciprocal-polynomial order has vertices (0,0),(2,1),(10,9),(12,12); adding the ten algebraic slopes gives the asserted multiset. The non-unit slopes rule out infinite height, and the slope-1/2 sector gives height two.
residual_risks: Ranks use Tate for K3 surfaces in characteristic 2 and refer to divisorial classes up to rank, not the integral intersection lattice. Mathematical correctness of the finding does not support its prior-work assertion.
